text: This is the capstone — one project pulling together everything from this course. You're going to take Northbridge Retail's product-catalog and checkout services and run them on Kubernetes the way a real platform team would. This lesson defines exactly what you're building, before you build it next lesson and present it in the one after.

Both services already exist as container images — product-catalog is a read-heavy API, checkout handles cart and order submission with spikier load. Your job is everything around those images: running them reliably, reachable from outside the cluster, configured correctly per environment, able to absorb a traffic spike, and deployed through a repeatable, versioned process instead of hand-run commands.

In scope: a Deployment, Service, and Ingress for each service; a ConfigMap and Secret for configuration and credentials; an HPA on checkout specifically, since it's the spiky one; the whole thing packaged as a Helm chart with per-environment values; and a short runbook for common failures.

Out of scope, deliberately: you're not writing product-catalog or checkout's application code, and you're not required to wire up a live GitOps controller end to end — you'll write the Argo CD manifest as a deliverable, but a real webhook-connected cluster is optional. Known boundaries are what make a capstone finishable.
Next lesson, we build every piece of this — charts, manifests, and the running cluster — step by step, verifying each layer before moving to the next.
